sdge:cc-dr-2026-04-01: This filing models the standard Schedule DR customer only: the Base Services Charge of $0.79343 per day, the flat EECC generation rate of $0.18274 per kWh, the eight UDC components, DWR-BC and WF-NBC, and the $0.10892 per kWh Baseline Adjustment Credit that produces the Tier 1 rate. Four published provisions are not represented. The DR-MB rate table on Sheet 2, whose total effective Medical Baseline rates are $0.32475 per kWh up to 130 percent of baseline and $0.41010 above it, with DWR-BC and WF-NBC not applying (note 3) and no Base Services Charge discount (note 6); no SDG&E Medical Baseline overlay exists in this corpus, so that customer class cannot be billed from the data at all. The Franchise Fee Differential of 5.78 percent applied to monthly billings for customers inside the corporate limits of the City of San Diego. The Direct Access and Community Choice Aggregation bill path of Special Condition 9.b, under which the EECC and DWR-BC components are credited back and the applicable Cost Responsibility Surcharge is added; the EECC that is modeled is the bundled rate, which per Special Condition 11 already embeds the Power Charge Indifference Adjustment. And the semi-annual California Climate Credit of $49.36 under Schedule GHG-ARR named in the applicability section. Separately, the two service tiers are bounded at a dimensionless 1.3 standing for 130 percent of the customer's allowance, so the Special Condition 3 allowance table itself (Basic Allowance 9.0, 10.4, 13.6 and 15.9 kWh per day in summer for the Coastal, Inland, Mountain and Desert zones and 9.2, 9.6, 12.9 and 10.9 in winter, with a separate All Electric set) is absent and a consumer must supply the customer's allowance to resolve the tier boundary. Two groups of provisions are out of scope rather than missing: the DR-LI (CARE) column and the DRAH and FERA Base Services Charges of $0.39688 per day are carried by separate overlay filings, and Special Conditions 1, 5, 6, 7 and 8 (load checks, standard lighting voltage, welder ratings, incidental farm service and common use service) are service-qualification and verification terms rather than rates.
sdge:cc-tou-dr1-2026-04-01: The most consequential gap is inside a charge the filing does model. Schedule TOU-DR1 publishes the Baseline Adjustment Credit as $(0.10892) per kWh for usage up to 130 percent of baseline, with the quantities given in Special Condition 15 (Basic Allowance 9.0, 10.4, 13.6 and 15.9 kWh per day in summer for the Coastal, Inland, Mountain and Desert zones and 9.2, 9.6, 12.9 and 10.9 in winter, plus a separate All Electric set), and Sheet 2 note (4) ties the credit to that cap. This filing carries the credit as a single price with no tier or bound, so it is applied to every kWh; a high-usage customer's bill computed from this data will be too low, and the published allowance quantities appear nowhere. Four further provisions are absent. The TOU-DR1-MB table on Sheet 3, whose total effective Medical Baseline rates run from $0.29919 per kWh summer super off-peak to $0.54054 summer on-peak with DWR-BC and WF-NBC at zero; no SDG&E Medical Baseline overlay exists in this corpus. The Franchise Fee Differential of 5.78 percent for customers within the corporate limits of the City of San Diego. The semi-annual California Climate Credit of $49.36 under Schedule GHG-ARR. And Special Condition 12 Bill Protection, a credit for the difference where a migrating customer's twelve-month total on this schedule exceeds what Schedule DR would have cost; note that the tariff closes this to new customers, stating that a customer taking service on or after March 1, 2019 does not receive it. The TOU-DR1-CARE column on Sheet 2 and the DRAH and FERA Base Services Charges of $0.39688 per day are carried by separate overlay filings rather than missing. Special Conditions 1, 6, 7, 8, 10 and 11 (interval metering, meter ownership and reads, multiple-account billing, standard lighting voltage and welder ratings) are metering and service terms, not rates; the Special Condition 9 bar on returning to the schedule for 12 months after leaving is an enrollment rule and is likewise not expressed.
sdge:cc-tou-dr-2026-04-01: Schedule TOU-DR publishes the Baseline Adjustment Credit as $(0.10892) per kWh for usage up to 130 percent of baseline, on both the Total Rates table and the UDC Rates table. This filing carries it as a single price with no tier or bound, so the credit is applied to every kWh and a high-usage customer's bill computed from this data will be too low. Unlike Schedule DR and Schedule TOU-DR1, this schedule does not itself publish the climate-zone allowance quantities, so the threshold has to come from elsewhere. Five further provisions are absent. The TOU-DR-MB table on Sheet 2, whose total effective Medical Baseline rates run from $0.35668 per kWh summer super off-peak to $0.48202 winter on-peak with DWR-BC and WF-NBC at zero; no SDG&E Medical Baseline overlay exists in this corpus. The Franchise Fee Differential of 5.78 percent for customers within the corporate limits of the City of San Diego. The Direct Access and Community Choice Aggregation bill path of Special Condition 2.b, which credits back the EECC component and adds the applicable Cost Responsibility Surcharge; the modeled EECC is the bundled rate, which per Special Condition 14 already embeds the Power Charge Indifference Adjustment. The semi-annual California Climate Credit of $49.36 under Schedule GHG-ARR. And Special Condition 10 Reconnection Charge, under which a customer resuming service within twelve months of discontinuing it pays all charges that would have been billed had service continued. Special Condition 11 requires twelve consecutive months on the schedule before switching and bars return for a year; neither the minimum tenure nor the return bar is expressed here, though the two EV schedules in this corpus do record their twelve-month minimum. The TOU-DR-LI (CARE) column and the DRAH and FERA Base Services Charges of $0.39688 per day are carried by separate overlay filings rather than missing, and Special Conditions 1, 3, 7, 8, 12 and 13 (interval metering, common use service, meter reads, multiple-account billing, standard lighting voltage and welder ratings) are service and metering terms rather than rates.
sdge:cc-ev-tou-2026-04-01: Schedule EV-TOU has no Base Services Charge; it uses a Minimum Bill of $0.413 per day, and the Sheet 2 Minimum Bill prose halves that to $0.207 per day for CARE, Medical Baseline and Family Electric Rate Assistance customers. This filing models the $0.413 standard rate only and carries the halved rate nowhere as a price. Its own price definition for the Minimum Bill states that the discounted rate is captured in the relevant modifier filings, and it is not: the SDG&E CARE and FERA overlay filings, both of which list this schedule among the plans they apply to, deliver a Base Services Charge adjustment, which is a charge this schedule does not have. A consumer composing those overlays onto this plan gets the wrong answer for the fixed portion of a low-income customer's bill. Three further provisions are absent. The Franchise Fee Differential of 5.78 percent for customers within the corporate limits of the City of San Diego. The Direct Access and Community Choice Aggregation bill path of Special Condition 7.b, which credits back the EECC and DWR-BC components and adds the applicable Cost Responsibility Surcharge; the modeled EECC is the bundled rate, which per Special Condition 9 already embeds the Power Charge Indifference Adjustment. And the Special Condition 4 bar on returning to the schedule for one year after leaving, where the twelve-month minimum stay from the same condition is recorded. Two provisions are out of scope rather than missing: Special Condition 6 Optional Billing, under which the utility may bill the lower of this schedule and the customer's otherwise applicable non-TOU schedule for three months, is solely at the utility's option and obligates it to nothing, and the Special Condition 2 requirement that the EV charging or CNG refueling facilities be separately metered is a metering arrangement rather than a rate.
sdge:cc-ev-tou-2-2026-04-01: Four provisions of the published Schedule EV-TOU-2 are not represented in this filing. The Franchise Fee Differential of 5.78 percent applied to monthly billings for all customers within the corporate limits of the City of San Diego. The semi-annual California Climate Credit of $49.36 under Schedule GHG-ARR, named in the applicability section. The Direct Access and Community Choice Aggregation bill path of Special Condition 8.b, under which the bill is computed as though bundled and then credited by the EECC and DWR-BC components, with the applicable Cost Responsibility Surcharge added; what is modeled is the bundled path, and its EECC rate per Special Condition 10 already embeds the Power Charge Indifference Adjustment. And the Special Condition 5 bar on returning to the schedule for one year after leaving, where the twelve-month minimum stay from the same condition is recorded. The Base Services Charge variants published on Sheets 1 and 2 for CARE ($0.19713 per day), FERA and DRAH ($0.39688 per day each) are carried by separate overlay filings rather than missing; the standard $0.79343 per day charge is modeled here. The remaining special conditions are out of scope rather than missing: standard lighting voltage (1), welder ratings (2), meter ownership and location (3), the fallback to the otherwise applicable domestic schedule when the meter's timing device fails (4), Optional Billing at the utility's sole option (7), and the requirement that a customer demonstrate eligibility to the utility's satisfaction (6) are service, metering and utility-discretion terms rather than rates.
sdge:cc-care-2025-10-01: This filing carries the four line-item pieces of the CARE benefit that are per-unit amounts: the Wildfire Fund Charge exemption ($0.00591 per kWh), the Department of Water Resources Bond Charge exemption (currently $0.00000), the CARE Surcharge exemption ($0.00864 per kWh) and the Base Services Charge reduction from $0.79343 to $0.19713 per day. The largest part of the benefit is missing. Sheet 1 sets the residential CARE discount at 35 percent as a fixed line-item discount pursuant to D.24-05-028, and Sheet 2 states it as 0.35000 applied to the total bill less applicable exemptions, minimum bill and base services charge; a URPX price is a per-unit dollar amount, and there is no way in this vocabulary to state a percentage of a computed bill, so nothing in the graph reflects it. Four further published provisions are absent. The alternative form of benefit (b) on Sheet 1, a 50 percent minimum bill in place of a reduced base services charge, which is the form the benefit takes on Schedule EV-TOU, a plan this overlay declares itself applicable to and which has a minimum bill rather than a base services charge. The $0.01062 per kWh CARE Surcharge for the DM and EV-TOU schedules, which is the rate Schedule EV-TOU takes under Sheet 2 note 2 (that note's 'All Other Residential CARE Schedules' list, which carries the $0.00864 rate modeled here, names DR, DS, DT, DT-RV, DR-SES, TOU-DR, EV-TOU-2, EV-TOU-5, TOU-DR1, TOU-DR2 and TOU-ELEC, and does not include EV-TOU). The Non-Residential CARE structure on Sheet 2, with its own 0.35000 discount and its own exemption list. And the Medical Baseline co-benefits that Sheet 2 extends to CARE Medical Baseline customers under Schedule E-MEDICAL, for which no filing exists in this corpus. Eligibility is expressed as residential customer kind plus enrollment in the CARE program, so the Special Condition 4 income table ($42,300 for a one or two person household rising to $108,300 for eight, plus $11,000 for each additional person) is not present as data. The remaining special conditions are out of scope rather than missing: application and recertification (2), commencement (3), verification (5), backbilling (6), notice of change (7), the above-400-percent-of-baseline documentation and 600 percent retention conditions (9), and the facility certification rules for non-profit group living, Homekey and agricultural employee housing (14 through 17) are program-administration procedures rather than rates.
sdge:cc-fera-2026-04-01: This filing carries one piece of the FERA benefit, the Base Services Charge reduction from $0.79343 to $0.39688 per day, modeled as a $0.39655 per day credit. The larger piece is missing: Sheet 1 grants a separate line-item bill discount of 18 percent applied to the total bill less any minimum bill amount or base services charge, and a URPX price is a per-unit dollar amount with no way to state a percentage of a computed bill, so nothing in the graph reflects it. Three further published provisions are absent. The alternative form of the fixed-charge benefit on Sheet 1, a 50 percent minimum bill in place of a reduced base services charge, which is the form it takes on Schedule EV-TOU, a plan this overlay declares itself applicable to and which has a $0.413 per day minimum bill rather than a base services charge. The Medical Baseline co-benefits that Sheet 1 extends to FERA Medical Baseline customers under Schedule E-MEDICAL pursuant to D.25-09-006, for which no filing exists in this corpus. And Special Condition 9 EV Submetering, under which the FERA discount applies to the submetered EV charging load as well as to the load at the primary meter where the equipment meets the D.22-08-024 submetering protocol. Eligibility is expressed as residential customer kind plus enrollment in the FERA program, so two published qualifying conditions are not present as data: the requirement of three or more persons in the household, and the Special Condition 1 income band ($42,301 to $52,875 for a one or two person household rising to $108,301 to $135,375 for eight, with $11,000 to $13,750 added per additional person, stated as 200 percent plus $1 through 250 percent of the Federal Poverty Limit). Special Conditions 2 through 6 (application and recertification, commencement, verification, notice of change, and rebilling for periods of ineligibility) are customer-administration procedures rather than rates, and their absence is a scope decision.
sdge:cc-nbt-2025-01-27: The per-hour export compensation surface is complete: 5,760 prices covering five vintages and both the generation and delivery components. What is missing is everything that settles over a period longer than one bill, plus one price that the source does not publish. The ACC Plus adder is declared as two price definitions, for the Residential and the Low Income Customer tiers, and carries no values; Special Condition 3.f refers to 'the ACC Plus credit' when describing what is excluded from the true-up comparison, but this composite PDF states no rate for it anywhere, so the gap is in the source as much as in the filing. The Relevant Period machinery of Special Conditions 3.d through 3.f is absent: twelve monthly billing cycles running from Permission To Operate and each anniversary, unused generation and delivery credits carried forward within that period, and excess export credits (ACC Plus excluded) zeroed out at true-up. Special Condition 6 Net Surplus Compensation is absent, both its energy value (net surplus kWh times SDG&E's Default Load Aggregation Point price, a rolling twelve-month average of DLAP prices from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. updated monthly) and the Renewable Attribute Adder paid when the customer certifies REC ownership, obtains CEC Renewables Portfolio Standard certification and transfers the certificates. The Special Condition 3.c limits on what credits may offset are also unrepresented: export credits may not offset monthly minimum charges, customer, meter, facilities or basic service charges, demand charges, non-bypassable charges or any fixed charge, and generation credits may offset only volumetric generation charges while delivery credits may offset only volumetric delivery charges. Three sub-schedule variants are out of scope here rather than missing, each being a distinct arrangement expected to be filed on its own: NBT Aggregation (Special Condition 12), NBT Paired Storage (Special Condition 8) and Multiple Tariff Facilities (Special Condition 5), as is the separately filed Schedule NBT-V for multi-tenant properties. So are the provisions that are not rates at all: the interconnection application forms and dates (4), the disaster provisions (10), the prevailing-wage obligations that attach to the installing contractor from the interconnection application onward (11), the consumer protection disclosure (9), and the Plug-in Electric Vehicle submetering exclusion (13).
